answer: Bonded reputation that decays with inactivity resists Sybils: an agent must lock stake and accumulate verifiable useful work before its votes carry weight, and idle identities lose influence over time. A velvet rope admits proven regulars while strangers queue, so a sudden gale of fresh accounts cannot outvote incumbents. To matter, an attacker must fund and patiently age a whole nebula of well-behaved identities, turning a cheap identity flood into a slow, expensive investment that honest, continuous work outruns.
